1.why: Modifier item: C is the only option whose subject is an animate agent that could have performed the withheld opening participle; A/B/D are passive or expletive evasions.

2.why: Perfectly symmetric their/its/they're/it's set with no internal asymmetry; betting the singular possessive because collective-noun-looks-plural is the commoner SEC design.

3.why: 'to satisfy' is the only option legal as a purpose/complement adjunct in most frames, but a gerund frame would make B legal too.

4.why: Three plural-agreeing options (were requiring, have required, require) against one singular; the lone singular is the number foil, so the key is the plain plural present.

5.why: Modifier item: C keeps 'the enormous mural' as subject; A swaps the agent, B buries it in an expletive, D shifts to a possessive sub-noun (the classic near-miss).

6.why: Aspect-only set with no number cue; betting the plain simple past as the narrative default.

7.why: Aspect-only set; 'cleared' is the plain form and the other three are all compound-aspect foils.

8.why: Key is the plain plural present: the remaining three then form the standard foil family of one number error (is) plus two tense/aspect errors (were, have been).

9.why: Key is the plain singular present: foils resolve to one number error (are) plus aspect/tense errors (has been, was).

10.why: Three singular forms against one plural; the plain singular present 'is' is the key and 'were' is the single number foil.

11.why: The set offers both ':' and ';' — if the following material were independent both would be legal, so it must be an explanation/fragment, which only the colon can introduce.

12.why: Plain-form bet again: 'collected' against a modal, a bare participle and a past-perfect progressive.

13.why: 'they' is the number foil; among the singulars I bet the option supplying an explicit coordinator, since a bare 'it' would splice.

14.why: 'one' and 'you' are person-shift foils and 'he' a number foil; betting the plural third person as the antecedent match.

15.why: Options are three marks plus no mark before a finite verb — no punctuation may ever separate a subject from its verb, so only the unpunctuated option is legal.

16.why: Comma-plus-coordinator is the only standard join here: bare comma splices, '; but' is nonstandard, ' but,' misplaces the mark.

17.why: Two plain forms available (present/past); betting simple present, with will/has-distributed as tense and aspect foils.

18.why: Plain plural present is the key; 'is' is the single number foil and were/have been the tense and aspect foils.

19.why: Symmetric their/its/it's/there set; same singular-possessive bet as item 2, with no asymmetry to break the tie.

20.why: C is a mangled active version of A (the archaeologist wrongly made the object), implying the intended frame names the archaeologist as agent with the scroll as main-clause subject.

21.why: A list follows; only a colon after a complete clause can introduce it — the comma, the 'being' participle and the '; and' are all illegal before a list.

22.why: 'nurses's' is impossible in any sentence, and its presence as a foil signals the item tests the plural possessive; plain plural and singular possessive are the other two foils.

23.why: Plain plural present is the key; 'is' is the single number foil, have been/were the aspect and tense foils.

24.why: Modifier item: C is the only option with the named person as subject, which is what a participial opener about analysing data requires.
